## Preliminaries

**Working scope (declared as assumption, not fact).** Hos 1:1-11 is taken as a single reading unit: superscription (v1) → the LORD's commission of Hosea's own sign-act marriage, with its stated reason (v2) → [v3 missing, see insufficiencies] → three symbolically-named children, each a further stated act of divine judgment against the house of Israel (vv4-9) → a restoration oracle that directly quotes and reverses the third child's name and the covenant-repudiation formula (vv10-11). "Bearing on the inner being" here is taken to include: (i) Hosea himself, the recipient of the word and the command's addressee (v1-2), whose own interior reaction to the command is nowhere stated (a recorded silence, see below); (ii) the LORD, the chapter's controlling divine voice, both commanding (vv2,4,6,9) and himself undergoing/enacting a change of disposition (withdrawing then, in the oracle, reversing, mercy and covenant-standing, vv6-7,9-10); (iii) "the land"/nation, indicted as already committing "whoredom" (v2) — the underlying unfaithfulness the sign-act enacts; (iv) Hosea's wife, present throughout (vv2-9) but, within this chapter's own surviving verse text, referred to only as "wife"/"she" — never named (her name and parentage come only from the missing v3, see insufficiencies); (v) the three children, each individually named as a stated act, each name itself carrying an indictment or (at the close) a reversal; (vi) the house of Israel and the house of Judah, addressed as contrasted collectives (mercy withdrawn from one, retained for the other, vv6-7) before being reunited in the closing oracle (v11).

**Reading rule applied.** No [AMBIGUOUS]-span STEP-live resolution was needed — the base extract reports 100% meaning coverage for this range (137/137 non-particle spans). Register shifts within the chapter: third-person narrative superscription (v1); narrated divine speech introducing the commission with its own reason-clause (v2); a structural gap where the narrated compliance would be (v3, missing); three repetitions of "the LORD said to him, 'Call his/her name X, for...'" each followed by a first-person divine judgment (vv4-9); a closing first-person-referenced restoration oracle in third-person narrative voice (vv10-11) that directly quotes v9's own words back before reversing them.

**Corpus-continuity check.** No prior filled debate found for this book at or before this range — this is the first debate in the sequence (or nothing precedes it yet). Nothing to re-read.

## Per-verse debate

### Hos 1:1

> The word of the Lord that came to Hosea, the son of Beeri, in the days of Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah, kings of Judah, and in the days of Jeroboam the son of Joash, king of Israel.

**Observation.** "The word [H1697G] of the LORD [H3068G] that came [to, H0413] to Hosea [H1954J], the son [H1121A] of Beeri [H0882H], in the days [H3117G] of Uzziah [H5818G], Jotham [H3147H], Ahaz [H0271G], and Hezekiah [H3169H], kings [H4428G] of Judah [H3063G], and in the days [H3117G] of Jeroboam [H3379H] the son [H1121A] of Joash [H3101J], king [H4428G] of Israel [H3478]."

**Operation 1 — the word of the LORD coming to be Hosea's own.**
- **Action-type:** came/was (the book's opening formula — the same bare-reception pattern as Joel 1:1/Jonah 1:1/Obad 1/Mic 1:1, though without Micah's added second act of "seeing").
- **Subject:** Hosea — named as the word's recipient, identified by patronymic (son of Beeri) alone; no further act is attributed to him in this verse.
- **Operation:** a state — the word simply "was" Hosea's (H1961, to be); no response, reaction, or seeing is described here (contrast Mic 1:1's added "which he saw").
- **Source:** the LORD, explicit.
- **Target:** n/a directly within this verse — the word's own content begins at v2.

**Interrogative — questions considered.**
- Q1/Q2: Hosea — a focused inner being in his own right as the word's recipient, though this verse itself states only bare reception, not an act of his own. The five named kings (Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz, Hezekiah, Jeroboam) and the two named fathers (Beeri, Joash) are not candidates here — no operation, state, or act is attributed to any of them; they function solely as a chronological/genealogical anchor, correctly set aside per step 3 note (a).
- Q3: The word's coming is stated explicitly, not inferred.
- Q4: Source = the LORD, explicit; no separate enablement is stated or needed for a bare reception.
- Q5: Target = n/a within this verse; the word's content is supplied from v2 onward.
- Q6: State — the word's bare coming.
- Q7: Forward linkage to the whole chapter: this verse supplies no content of its own, only the frame within which vv2-11 unfold.
- Q8: N/A this verse.
- Q9: Sufficient for what is stated; nothing about Hosea's own interior at the moment of reception is given (contrast Micah's explicit "seeing").
- Q11: came/was.

**Decision.** Retain as the book's formal opening. The named kings/fathers are set aside (no operation stated).

### Hos 1:2

> When the Lord first spoke through Hosea, the Lord said to Hosea, “ Go, take to yourself a wife of whoredom and have children of whoredom, for the land commits great whoredom by forsaking the Lord.”

**Observation.** "When the LORD [H3068G] first [H8462] spoke [H1696G] through [in/on/with, H9003] Hosea [H1954J], the LORD [H3068G] said [H0559] to [H0413] Hosea [H1954J], 'Go [H1980G], take [H3947I] to yourself a wife [H0802H] of whoredom [H2183] and have children [H3206] of whoredom [H2183], for [H3588A] the land [H0776G] commits great whoredom [to fornicate, H2181/H3588A] by forsaking [after, from, H0310A/H9006] the LORD [H3068G].'"

**Operation 1 — the LORD's own initial speaking through Hosea.**
- **Action-type:** spoke/began (a commissioning formula, distinct from and prior to the specific command that follows).
- **Subject:** the LORD; Hosea is named as the channel ("through Hosea") but not yet given an act of his own.
- **Operation:** a movement — the LORD's word beginning to be spoken, marked explicitly as "first" (H8462), i.e. this is the book's inaugural prophetic utterance.
- **Source:** the LORD, self.
- **Target:** Hosea, as the channel through which the word reaches its ultimate audience (the land/nation, named later in this same verse).

**Operation 2 — the LORD's direct command to Hosea: take a wife of whoredom, have children of whoredom.**
- **Action-type:** commanded (a sign-act commission, imperative mood: "Go, take... and have...").
- **Subject:** Hosea, the command's addressee; his own compliance is not narrated in this range (see insufficiencies — the compliance verse, v3, is missing from iba.db).
- **Operation:** a movement demanded of Hosea (go, take, have) — a stated future act, not yet an accomplished one within this verse.
- **Source:** the LORD, explicit and direct.
- **Target:** the not-yet-named woman ("a wife of whoredom") and the not-yet-born "children of whoredom" — both introduced only by category, not by name, within this verse.

**Operation 3 — the land's own committed unfaithfulness (the command's stated reason).**
- **Action-type:** forsook/fornicated (a collective's own already-ongoing operation, stated as the ground for Operation 2's command).
- **Subject:** "the land" (H0776G) — a collective standing for the nation (Q8), not an individual.
- **Operation:** a movement — "forsaking" (H0310A/H9006, literally "from after") the LORD, described as already in progress ("commits," a participial/verbal form indicating a continuing state), not a single past act.
- **Source:** self — the land's own committed unfaithfulness, not attributed to any outside enabler.
- **Target:** the LORD — the one forsaken; the relationship itself is the object of the land's own operation.

**Interrogative — questions considered.**
- Q1/Q2: Hosea is a focused inner being, but this verse states only what he is commanded to do, not his own disposition toward the command — an interior is invited by the shocking content of the command but not itself supplied (see silence, below). The land/nation is likewise a focused collective interior, given explicit stated content ("commits... whoredom... forsaking") rather than left to inference.
- Q3: The command itself and the land's unfaithfulness are both stated explicitly. Hosea's own interior response to receiving so unusual a command is not stated at all — a recorded silence (Part B.4), not filled from outside knowledge of how such commissions are elsewhere described.
- Q4: Source of the command = the LORD, explicit. Source of the land's own unfaithfulness = self (its own forsaking), explicit — the two sources kept distinct: the LORD sources the command to Hosea; the land sources its own prior infidelity, which the command is a response to, not a cause of.
- Q5: Target of the command = the not-yet-named wife/children; target of the land's forsaking = the LORD himself.
- Q6: Movement throughout — the word's speaking (Op 1), the commanded taking (Op 2), the land's ongoing forsaking (Op 3, a continuing movement away).
- Q7: Forward linkage — "wife of whoredom" and "children of whoredom" are each given a name and a specific indictment in vv4-9; the land's own "whoredom" (v2) is the interpretive key the whole chapter's naming-sequence enacts (Hosea's marriage is explicitly stated to mirror the nation's own unfaithfulness, not left to inference). This is close to, but broader than, Q12's shared-vocabulary anchor — a whole-book structural mirroring, not a single juxtaposed pair of operations; logged as an emergent question below rather than asserted as a formal Q12 instance.
- Q8: "The land" — the nation as a collective; its unfaithfulness is treated as a corporate condition, not itemised individual acts.
- Q9: Sufficient for what is stated; Hosea's own interior at the point of command is not supplied — named as insufficiency, not inferred.
- Q11: spoke/began (Op 1); commanded (Op 2); forsook/fornicated (Op 3).

**Decision.** Retain all three operations. Hosea's own silent interior is recorded as a silence, not filled. The land's stated unfaithfulness is retained as the chapter's interpretive ground.

**Verse gap -- by design.** `Hosea 1:3` has no verse row in iba.db (no onboarded term's concordance search ever surfaced it -- see governance.verse_gap_by_design). Not an error; continuing with the next available verse. **Note beyond the standard gap notice:** this specific missing verse (the narrated compliance — "So he went and took Gomer, the daughter of Diblaim...") is the ONLY place in the received text where Hosea's wife is named. Its absence means that within this chapter's surviving data, she is never named at all — see insufficiencies register.

### Hos 1:4

> And the Lord said to him, “ Call his name Jezreel, for in just a little while I will punish the house of Jehu for the blood of Jezreel, and I will put an end to the kingdom of the house of Israel.

**Observation.** "And the LORD [H3068G] said [H0559] to [H0413] him, 'Call [H7121H] his name [H8034] Jezreel [H3157K], for [H3588A] in just a little [H4592] while [H5750] I will punish [H6485H] the house [H1004M] of Jehu [H3058H] for [upon, H5921A] the blood [H1818] of Jezreel [H3157K], and I will put an end [H7673A] to the kingdom [H4468] of the house [H1004M] of Israel [H3478].'"

**Operation 1 — the LORD's naming-command for the first son.**
- **Action-type:** named/commanded (surface act: a naming instruction; the operation hidden behind it, per step 3 note (e), is the divine indictment the name itself encodes).
- **Subject:** Hosea, the addressee of the command; the child himself is the one named, not yet an operative subject in his own right.
- **Operation:** a movement — the commanded act of naming.
- **Source:** the LORD.
- **Target:** the son, receiving the name "Jezreel" — a name that is itself an indictment (see Operation 2).

**Operation 2 — the LORD's stated coming punishment of the house of Jehu.**
- **Action-type:** punish (a declared future judicial act).
- **Subject:** the LORD, self.
- **Operation:** a movement — a stated future act ("in just a little while"), not yet accomplished within the verse.
- **Source:** self, explicit ("I will punish").
- **Target:** "the house of Jehu" — a dynastic collective (Q8), indicted "for the blood of Jezreel" — a referential allusion (Part B.3) to Jehu's own violent seizure of the throne at Jezreel (2 Kings 9-10), not narrated within this base extract itself but presupposed by the naming.
- **Insufficiency:** the base extract carries no record of the Jehu/Jezreel massacre it refers to; the allusion is named as such, not supplied as fact from outside knowledge beyond identifying that the reference exists.

**Operation 3 — the LORD's stated termination of the kingdom of the house of Israel.**
- **Action-type:** ended/terminated.
- **Subject:** the LORD, self.
- **Operation:** a movement — a further declared future act.
- **Source:** self.
- **Target:** "the kingdom of the house of Israel" — the northern kingdom as a whole (Q8, broader than Operation 2's specific dynasty).

**Interrogative — questions considered.**
- Q1/Q2: Hosea, addressed but not given his own stated interior here. The house of Jehu and the house of Israel are both collectives with a clearly stated interior-relevant status: under active divine judgment.
- Q3: Both punishments are stated explicitly as the LORD's own future acts; the historical allusion behind "blood of Jezreel" is named as referential, not filled in from outside the base extract.
- Q4: Source of both judgments = the LORD, self, explicit; no human enabler stated.
- Q5: Target of Operation 2 = house of Jehu (a dynasty); target of Operation 3 = house of Israel (the wider kingdom) — a narrowing-then-widening structure worth noting.
- Q6: Movement throughout (declared future acts).
- Q7: Direct linkage forward to v5 (further judgment "on that day," same Jezreel location) and to v11 (Jezreel's name recurs a third time, there reversed to a positive "day of Jezreel").
- Q8: House of Jehu (a ruling dynasty) and house of Israel (the whole northern kingdom) — both collectives, the second broader than the first.
- Q9: Sufficient for what is stated; the historical background to "blood of Jezreel" is not itself supplied by the base extract — named, not assumed.
- Q11: named/commanded (Op 1); punish (Op 2); ended/terminated (Op 3).

**Decision.** Retain all three operations. The Jehu allusion is retained with its historical background explicitly flagged as outside this base extract's data (insufficiency, not filled).

### Hos 1:5

> And on that day I will break the bow of Israel in the Valley of Jezreel.”

**Observation.** "And on that day [H3117G/H9003/H1961] I will break [H7665/H1931/H9009] the bow [H7198/H0853] of Israel [H3478] in [H9003] the Valley [H6010M] of Jezreel [H3157L]."

**Operation 1 — the LORD's own act of disabling Israel's military strength.**
- **Action-type:** broke (a decisive, single military-symbolic act).
- **Subject:** the LORD, self.
- **Operation:** a movement — a further declared future act, continuing directly from v4 ("on that day").
- **Source:** self, explicit.
- **Target:** "the bow of Israel" — a symbol (metonymy) for the nation's military capacity as a whole (Q8, the collective's strength rather than an individual weapon).

**Interrogative — questions considered.**
- Q1/Q2: No human individual is in focus; Israel is addressed as a collective military capacity, its "state" here being its (soon to be broken) strength.
- Q3: Stated explicitly, continuing v4's declared judgment.
- Q4: Source = the LORD, self; no enabler needed or stated.
- Q5: Target = Israel's own military capacity ("the bow"), a collective possession rather than a person.
- Q6: Movement — a decisive future breaking.
- Q7: Direct linkage back to v4 ("that day," same judgment continuing) and forward to v7, where "bow" recurs explicitly as one of the means by which Judah will NOT be saved — the identical term used first as the object of Israel's judgment (broken, v5) then as a rejected means even for Judah's own deliverance (v7): the same word doing double duty within one chapter for two contrasted collectives, both operations belonging to the LORD (not a Q12 human-vs-divine instance, but a genuine intra-divine lexical recurrence worth tracking, comparable to Micah 1's "come down" and Micah 4's "gather" recurrences).
- Q8: Israel, as a national military collective.
- Q9: Sufficient for what is stated.
- Q11: broke.

**Decision.** Retain. Flagged for the passage-level linkages as the chapter's clearest intra-divine lexical recurrence ("bow," vv5/7).

### Hos 1:6

> She conceived again and bore a daughter. And the Lord said to him, “ Call her name No Mercy, for I will no more have mercy on the house of Israel, to forgive them at all.

**Observation.** "She conceived [H2029] again [H5750] and bore [H3205] a daughter [H1323G]. And the LORD [H3068G] said [H0559] to him, 'Call [H7121H] her name [H8034] No Mercy [H3819], for [H3588A] I will no [H3808] more [H3254G] have mercy [H7355/H5750] on the house [H1004M/H0853] of Israel [H3478], to forgive [H5375I/H3588A] them at all [H5375I].'"

**Operation 1 — Hosea's wife's own bearing of a daughter.**
- **Action-type:** conceived/bore.
- **Subject:** "she" — Hosea's wife, present throughout this chapter but, within this chapter's own surviving text, never given a name (her name, Gomer, and her father's name, Diblaim, occur only in the missing v3 — see insufficiencies). She is identified here only by the pronoun and by the marital/maternal role.
- **Operation:** a state/movement — conception and childbirth, narrated in bare third-person report, with no stated interior of her own (no reaction, consent, or disposition given at any point in this chapter — a further silence, alongside Hosea's own at v2).
- **Source:** self, in the sense that the bearing is her own bodily act; the marriage itself (its source and its "whoredom" framing) was established at v2 and is not re-argued here.
- **Target:** n/a directly; the daughter is the operation's own result, immediately taken up as the subject of Operation 2.

**Operation 2 — the LORD's naming-command for the daughter.**
- **Action-type:** named/commanded, structurally identical to v4's pattern.
- **Subject:** Hosea, addressee; the daughter, named.
- **Operation:** a movement — the commanded naming act.
- **Source:** the LORD.
- **Target:** the daughter, receiving the name "No Mercy" (Lo-ruhamah).

**Operation 3 — the LORD's own stated withdrawal of mercy from the house of Israel.**
- **Action-type:** withdrew/refused (a stated change, or at least a stated cessation, of a divine interior disposition — not merely an external act, but mercy itself, withheld).
- **Subject:** the LORD, self.
- **Operation:** a state — an explicit divine disposition ("I will no more have mercy... to forgive them at all") stated directly, not inferred; this is one of the chapter's clearest instances of a divine interior state being named as such, rather than only an external judicial act (contrast vv4-5's acts of punishing/breaking).
- **Source:** self; the LORD's own decision, not attributed to or blamed on any external cause.
- **Target:** "the house of Israel" — the collective (Q8) whose covenant standing is directly affected by this stated withdrawal of divine disposition, not merely its circumstances (Part B.5 — here the text itself extends sourcing from an act into the LORD's own interior disposition, unusually direct).

**Interrogative — questions considered.**
- Q1/Q2: The wife is a focused inner being in her own right (a human person, not merely a plot device), yet the text gives her no stated interior at any point in this chapter — named as a silence, not filled from assumption about how she might have felt. The LORD's own interior (withdrawn mercy) is, by contrast, stated with unusual directness.
- Q3: The wife's conceiving/bearing is stated (an external act); her name comes from a missing verse, so treated here as referential/inferred from the wider base data (the person-lexicon entries for the children elsewhere in this same extract identify her as "Gomer" in their own background notes) rather than from this chapter's own verse text — named as such per Q3/note (e), not asserted as though the chapter itself said it. The LORD's withdrawal of mercy is stated explicitly, not inferred.
- Q4: Source of the wife's bearing = herself, bodily; source of the LORD's withdrawn mercy = himself, explicit and direct.
- Q5: Target of Operation 3 = the house of Israel, its covenant standing.
- Q6: State/movement (bearing); state (the LORD's withdrawn disposition, the chapter's clearest interior-state statement so far).
- Q7: Direct linkage forward to v7 (immediate contrast: mercy withdrawn from Israel here, retained for Judah there) and to v9-10 (the third child's name/reversal follows the identical naming-then-indictment structure, then is itself directly quoted and reversed).
- Q8: House of Israel, the collective whose standing is affected.
- Q9: Sufficient for what is stated; the wife's own name and interior are both named as missing/silent, not supplied.
- Q11: conceived/bore (Op 1); named/commanded (Op 2); withdrew/refused (Op 3).

**Decision.** Retain all three operations. The wife's un-named status within this chapter's own text, and both her and Hosea's un-stated interiors, are recorded as insufficiencies/silences, not filled.

### Hos 1:7

> But I will have mercy on the house of Judah, and I will save them by the Lord their God. I will not save them by bow or by sword or by war or by horses or by horsemen.”

**Observation.** "But I will have mercy [H7355] on the house [H1004M/H0853] of Judah [H3063G], and I will save [H3467] them by the LORD [H3068G] their God [H0430G]. I will not [H3808] save [H3467] them by bow [H7198] or by sword [H2719] or by war [H4421] or by horses [H5483M] or by horsemen [H6571B]."

**Operation 1 — the LORD's own retained mercy toward the house of Judah.**
- **Action-type:** had-mercy/saved (a direct contrast to v6's withdrawal).
- **Subject:** the LORD, self.
- **Operation:** a state — mercy retained, stated as directly as v6's withdrawal was, the two verses forming a single deliberate contrast between the two covenant collectives.
- **Source:** self.
- **Target:** "the house of Judah" — the contrasted collective (Q8) to v6's "house of Israel."

**Operation 2 — the LORD's stated mode of Judah's salvation: himself, not military means.**
- **Action-type:** saved/refused (a double-sided statement: what the salvation IS attributed to, and what it explicitly is NOT).
- **Subject:** the LORD, self, twice over ("I will save... I will not save... by bow... sword... war... horses... horsemen").
- **Operation:** a movement (an act of deliverance) explicitly distinguished from a list of conventional military means, all five explicitly negated.
- **Source:** self, directly — "by the LORD their God," not by any instrument.
- **Target:** the house of Judah, the same collective as Operation 1.

**Interrogative — questions considered.**
- Q1/Q2: No new human individual in focus; the house of Judah, as a collective, is the recipient of a stated divine disposition (mercy retained) exactly parallel in form to v6's withdrawal from Israel.
- Q3: Stated explicitly, in direct grammatical contrast to v6 ("but I will have mercy," immediately following "I will no more have mercy").
- Q4: Source = the LORD, self, explicitly and emphatically NOT any of the five listed military means — an unusually direct case of the text itself foreclosing an alternative-enablement reading (Part B.5).
- Q5: Target = the house of Judah.
- Q6: State (mercy retained) and movement (the act of saving, defined negatively against military means).
- Q7: **Major linkage, shared term, not a Q12 instance.** "Bow" (H7198) recurs from v5, where it was the object of Israel's own judgment (broken); here it is one of five rejected means even for Judah's favoured deliverance — the identical term serving two purposes for two contrasted collectives within one chapter, both operations belonging to the LORD (not a human-vs-divine mirror, so not formally Q12), comparable in shape to Micah's own "gather"/"come down" intra-divine recurrences. Also a direct verse-pair contrast with v6 (mercy withdrawn/retained, the chapter's most explicit twinned divine-disposition statement).
- Q8: House of Judah, the collective.
- Q9: Sufficient for what is stated.
- Q11: had-mercy/saved (Op 1); saved/refused (Op 2).

**Decision.** Retain both operations. Flagged in the passage-level linkages as the chapter's clearest twinned contrast (vv6-7) and its clearest intra-divine lexical recurrence ("bow," vv5/7).

### Hos 1:8

- **Operation:** a state/movement — a bare narrated sequence of maternal acts, again with no stated interior of her own.

- Q3: Stated explicitly (the acts themselves); her name/interior remain unstated/inferred as before.

### Hos 1:9

> And the Lord said, “ Call his name Not My People, for you are not my people, and I am not your God.”

**Observation.** "And the LORD [H3068G] said [H0559], 'Call [H7121H] his name [H8034] Not My People [H3818], for [H3588A] you [H0859D] are not [H3808] my [H9020] people [H5971A], and I [H0595] am [H1961] not [H3808] your [H9036] God [n/a explicit — supplied by ellipsis in the Hebrew, per the clause's own parallel structure].'"

**Operation 1 — the LORD's naming-command for the third child.**
- **Action-type:** named/commanded, structurally identical to vv4/6.
- **Subject:** the LORD, commanding (addressee unspecified here, unlike vv4/6's explicit "to him" — a minor structural variation).
- **Operation:** a movement — the commanded naming act.
- **Source:** the LORD.
- **Target:** the son, named "Not My People" (Lo-ammi).

**Operation 2 — the LORD's own declared repudiation of the covenant relationship itself.**
- **Action-type:** repudiated/un-named (a formal, mutual covenant-formula inversion: the Sinai covenant formula, "you shall be my people, and I will be your God," is here directly negated on both sides).
- **Subject:** the LORD, self — the more consequential of the chapter's two parties to this declaration, since it is his own disposition being restated as withdrawn.
- **Operation:** a state — a declared covenant status, negated on both sides at once ("you are not my people, and I am not your God"), the chapter's most formally structured statement of relational rupture.
- **Source:** self, the LORD's own declaration; though the naming's stated reason ("for") makes the addressed party's own prior status ("you") jointly responsible — both sides of the formula are stated, not only the LORD's.
- **Target:** "you" — grammatically addressed to the child being named but referentially reaching past the child to Israel itself (an inferred/referential widening, per note (e), consistent with each of the three children's names throughout this chapter).

**Interrogative — questions considered.**
- Q1/Q2: The addressed "you" (Israel, referentially) is a focused collective whose covenant standing is the operation's own content, stated directly rather than inferred.
- Q3: Stated explicitly — both halves of the covenant-formula inversion are given in the LORD's own words. The referential widening from "the child" to "Israel" is named as inference (note (e)), not asserted as though the verse names Israel directly.
- Q4: Source = the LORD, self, explicit on both sides of the declaration.
- Q5: Target = the addressed "you" (Israel), the relationship itself the object of the declared change.
- Q6: State — a declared, mutual covenant-status change.
- Q7: **Direct forward linkage, the chapter's most explicit lexical reversal.** The exact phrase "not my people" is quoted verbatim at v10 and there directly reversed ("in the place where it was said to them, 'you are not my people,' it shall be said to them, 'children of the living God'") — an intra-divine self-quotation-and-reversal, not a human-vs-divine mirror (so not a formal Q12 instance; both the original declaration and its reversal are the LORD's own words), but the single clearest instance of the LORD's own operation being directly cited then undone anywhere in this chapter. Logged as a distinct pattern in the emergent questions below (intra-divine self-reversal, as opposed to Q12's human-vs-divine comparison, or Micah's plain intra-divine vocabulary recurrence without reversal).
- Q8: The addressed "you," referentially Israel as a collective.
- Q9: Sufficient for what is stated; the referential widening from child's-name to nation is named as such.
- Q11: named/commanded (Op 1); repudiated/un-named (Op 2).

**Decision.** Retain both operations. The covenant-formula inversion (Op 2) and its v10 reversal are flagged as the chapter's central structural hinge.

### Hos 1:10

> Yet the number of the children of Israel shall be like the sand of the sea, which cannot be measured or numbered. And in the place where it was said to them, “You are not my people,” it shall be said to them, “ Children of the living God.”

**Observation.** "Yet the number [H4557/H1961] of the children [H1121G] of Israel [H3478] shall be like [H9004] the sand [H2344] of the sea [H3220G], which [H0834A] cannot be measured [H4058/H3808] or numbered [H5608A/H3808/H9002]. And in [H9003] the place [H4725/H1961] where [H0834A] it was said [H0559] to them, 'You [H0859D] are not [H3808] my [H9020] people [H5971A],' it shall be said [H0559] to them, 'Children [H1121G] of the living [H2416A] God [H0410G].'"

**Operation 1 — the LORD's own promise of Israel's future numerical increase.**
- **Action-type:** promised/increased (a stated future reversal of scale, echoing — referentially, per Part B.3, not stated within this verse itself — the Abrahamic increase-promise idiom "as the sand of the sea," Gen 22:17/32:12).
- **Subject:** the LORD, implicitly (the promise's own source, though the verb here is passive/stative — "shall be" — rather than a direct first-person declaration as in vv4-9).
- **Operation:** a state/movement — a declared future condition ("shall be like the sand of the sea... cannot be measured"), a direct numerical reversal of the covenant-rupture just declared.
- **Source:** the LORD (by continuation from vv4-9's pattern, though not restated as "I" within this verse); the referential link to the Abrahamic promise is named as an intertextual echo, not asserted as this verse's own explicit content.
- **Target:** "the children of Israel," the same collective whose kingdom was ended at v4-5.

**Operation 2 — the LORD's own direct reversal of the third child's name/declaration (v9 quoted and undone).**
- **Action-type:** reversed/renamed (a self-quotation followed immediately by its own negation).
- **Subject:** the LORD, self (the same party who made the original declaration at v9).
- **Operation:** a state — the identical phrase "you are not my people" is quoted verbatim, then directly answered by "children of the living God," a formal, deliberate undoing of v9's own covenant-repudiation, in the same location ("in the place where it was said... it shall be said").
- **Source:** self — the LORD's own prior declaration, now itself reversed by the same voice.
- **Target:** "them" — the same addressed party as v9, i.e. Israel, referentially.

**Interrogative — questions considered.**
- Q1/Q2: Israel (the children of Israel), a focused collective, given a stated future condition directly answering its own immediately-prior stated rupture (v9).
- Q3: Stated explicitly, as a direct quotation-then-reversal; the Abrahamic-promise echo is named as intertextual/referential, not part of this verse's own explicit statement.
- Q4: Source = the LORD, by continuation of the pattern, though the verb form here is less directly first-person than vv4-9 — worth naming as a minor shift in voice, not resolved further.
- Q5: Target = the children of Israel/"them," the same party as v9.
- Q6: State (future condition) and a formal self-reversal (movement from one declared status to its opposite).
- Q7: **The chapter's most direct self-reversal, continuing from v9.** "Not my people" (v9) is quoted verbatim, then immediately replaced by "children of the living God" — an intra-divine self-quotation-and-reversal (the same voice undoing its own prior declaration), distinct from a Q12 human-vs-divine mirror (no human operation is being compared here) and distinct from Micah's plain intra-divine vocabulary recurrence without reversal (e.g. "come down," "gather") — logged below as its own emergent pattern.
- Q8: The children of Israel, a collective.
- Q9: Sufficient for what is stated; the Abrahamic-promise echo is named as referential background, not filled in as though stated here.
- Q11: promised/increased (Op 1); reversed/renamed (Op 2).

**Decision.** Retain both operations. The v9/v10 reversal is the chapter's structural climax; flagged fully in passage-level linkages and the emergent questions log.

### Hos 1:11

> And the children of Judah and the children of Israel shall be gathered together, and they shall appoint for themselves one head. And they shall go up from the land, for great shall be the day of Jezreel.

**Observation.** "And the children [H1121G] of Judah [H3063G] and the children [H1121G] of Israel [H3478] shall be gathered together [H6908], and they shall appoint [H7760L] for themselves one [H0259] head [H7218H], and they shall go up [H5927G] from [H4480A] the land [H0776G], for [H3588A] great [H1419A] shall be the day [H3117G] of Jezreel [H3157H]."

**Operation 1 — the reunification of Judah and Israel.**
- **Action-type:** gathered (a restorative reversal of vv6-7's contrasted, separately-treated collectives).
- **Subject:** "the children of Judah and the children of Israel" — the two collectives distinguished throughout the chapter (mercy withdrawn from one, retained for the other, vv6-7), now reunited as a single acting party.
- **Operation:** a movement — a stated future gathering-together, resolving the chapter's Judah/Israel contrast.
- **Source:** the passive verb form leaves the immediate agent unstated (they "shall be gathered"), though by continuation of the chapter's pattern the LORD remains the implied ultimate source; this is named as a minor grammatical shift, not resolved further within this base extract.
- **Target:** n/a directly; the two collectives are both subject and, implicitly, the recipients of the gathering.

**Operation 2 — the reunified people's own self-directed political act: appointing one head.**
- **Action-type:** appointed (a self-directed act, notably NOT stated as a direct divine installation).
- **Subject:** the reunited "children of Judah and Israel," now acting as a single collective agent.
- **Operation:** a movement — "they shall appoint for themselves" (H9038, "to/for them" — reflexive), a self-sourced political act.
- **Source:** self — the people's own choice, explicitly reflexive ("for themselves"), in contrast to vv4-5's and v9's divine acts done directly TO the nation without any stated human agency of its own; worth flagging as a genuine shift in whose operation is in view, from the LORD acting on Israel to Israel acting for itself.
- **Target:** "one head" — a single appointed leader, the object of their own collective choice.

**Operation 3 — the people's own going-up from the land.**
- **Action-type:** ascended/departed.
- **Subject:** the reunited collective, continuing as Operation 2's subject.
- **Operation:** a movement — "go up from the land," language elsewhere associated with return-from-exile or ascent (referential, not itself further specified within this verse).
- **Source:** self, continuing the collective's own agency from Operation 2.
- **Target:** n/a directly stated; the movement's destination is not given within this verse.

**Interrogative — questions considered.**
- Q1/Q2: The reunited Judah/Israel collective, given, for the first time in this chapter, a stated act of its OWN agency (appointing, going up) rather than only being acted upon.
- Q3: Stated explicitly, though the ultimate source of the initial "gathering" (passive voice) is not restated as directly as vv4-9's first-person divine declarations — named as a structural observation, not resolved by inference.
- Q4: Source of the gathering = ambiguous/passive, by continuation likely the LORD; source of the appointing and going-up = the people themselves, explicitly reflexive — a genuine shift in agency worth surfacing, not collapsing the two into one source.
- Q5: Target = n/a directly stated for any of the three operations within this verse.
- Q6: Movement throughout (gathering, appointing, ascending).
- Q7: **Direct linkage, a third recurrence of "Jezreel," valence reversed.** "Jezreel" recurs a third time in this chapter (vv4, 5, 11) — at vv4-5 the name and location of judgment (the house of Jehu's bloodguilt, Israel's broken bow); here, at the chapter's close, "great shall be the DAY of Jezreel" — the identical place-name now carrying a positive valence, closing the chapter's naming-then-reversal structure (matching v9-10's "not my people"/"children of the living God" reversal, and the first child's own name, Jezreel, reversed in kind). Also linked to v10's collective-increase promise, both closing the chapter on restoration.
- Q8: The reunited Judah/Israel, a single collective formed from two previously-contrasted ones.
- Q9: Sufficient for what is stated; the destination of "go up from the land" is not given.
- Q11: gathered (Op 1); appointed (Op 2); ascended/departed (Op 3).

**Decision.** Retain all three operations. Flagged as the chapter's closing reversal, structurally paired with v9-10 and completing the threefold Jezreel recurrence (vv4/5/11).

## Passage-level linkages (Q7)

1. **The threefold "Jezreel" recurrence (vv4, 5, 11), valence reversed at the close.** Judgment-location (vv4-5, the house of Jehu's bloodguilt, Israel's broken military strength) becomes, by the same name, the site of a "great day" at v11 — the chapter's clearest single-word structural frame.
2. **The v9/v10 direct self-quotation-and-reversal ("not my people" → "children of the living God").** The chapter's most explicit instance of the LORD directly quoting his own prior declaration and undoing it in the same breath — an intra-divine self-reversal, distinct from both Q12 (no human operation is compared) and from a plain intra-divine vocabulary recurrence without reversal (contrast "bow," below).
3. **"Bow" (H7198), recurring vv5/7, not reversed but repurposed.** Israel's own military bow is broken in judgment (v5); the identical term returns at v7 as one of five rejected MEANS even for Judah's own salvation — the same word doing different work for two contrasted collectives, both instances the LORD's own operation (not Q12).
4. **The vv6-7 twinned contrast (mercy withdrawn from Israel / retained for Judah).** The chapter's most direct back-to-back statement of a divine interior disposition, applied oppositely to two named collectives in consecutive verses.
5. **Whole-chapter structural mirroring (Hosea's own marriage enacting the nation's unfaithfulness).** Explicitly stated as the command's own reason at v2 ("for the land commits great whoredom"), this is not a single-verse Q12 instance (no shared verb/vocabulary anchor within one juxtaposed pair) but a whole-chapter enactment — Hosea's own sign-act marriage standing for the LORD's own relationship to Israel. Logged as an emergent question (below) about whether Q12 as currently scoped (textually-anchored, verb-shared) is the right instrument for a structural/typological mirroring of this kind, or whether it needs a named companion category.

## Insufficiencies register

1. **Hos 1:3 (the compliance/marriage verse) is entirely missing from iba.db** (verse-existence gap, by design per governance ruling). Consequence: within this chapter's own surviving text, Hosea's wife is never named — her name (Gomer) and father's name (Diblaim) exist in the base data only as background notes attached to the children's own person-lexicon entries (e.g. under H3157K, "Jezreel"), not as the verse's own stated text. Treated throughout as referential, not as this chapter's own direct statement.
2. **Hosea's own interior reaction to the command (v2) is never stated** — no verse in this range records his compliance, reluctance, or disposition toward marrying "a wife of whoredom." Recorded as a silence (Part B.4), not filled from outside assumption.
3. **The wife's own interior across all three childbirths (vv6, 8, and implicitly v2-3) is never stated** — no consent, reaction, or disposition is given at any point in the surviving text.
4. **The historical background presupposed by "the blood of Jezreel" (v4) — Jehu's own violent seizure of the throne, 2 Kings 9-10 — is not itself part of this base extract.** Named as an allusion the chapter's own indictment depends on, not supplied as fact from outside the base data.
5. **The Abrahamic increase-promise idiom ("as the sand of the sea," v10) is an intertextual echo, not confirmed within this base extract as a deliberate citation** — named as likely background, not asserted as the verse's own stated intent.

## Emergent questions log (filed against this passage — not merged across passages; resolved, if at all, at the whole-book read)

- **EQ1.** Does Q12 (divine mirroring, textually-anchored by shared vocabulary within one juxtaposed pair) adequately capture Hosea's OWN central device — a whole-chapter, indeed likely whole-book, structural enactment where a human's own life (Hosea's marriage) is explicitly stated to mirror the divine-human relationship, without any single shared verb anchoring it the way Micah 2:1/3's "devise/devise" or Obadiah 15's "as you have done, it shall be done to you" do? Carried forward as a live question for the rest of this book, since it may recur chapter by chapter as Hosea's marriage/family continues to be referenced (see chapter 2/3 when read).
- **EQ2.** Is the v9/v10 pattern — the LORD directly quoting and reversing his OWN prior declaration — a distinct category worth tracking alongside Q12 (human-vs-divine mirroring) and the already-noted intra-divine vocabulary recurrence without reversal (Micah's "come down," this chapter's own "bow")? This chapter supplies the clearest example yet of a third, self-reversal shape. Carried forward to the whole-book read and future chapters/books.
- **EQ3.** The wife's complete namelessness and silence within this chapter's own surviving text (contrast the missing v3, which alone would have supplied her name) — worth watching whether later chapters (2, 3) supply any stated interior for her at all, or whether her silence is sustained throughout the book as a deliberate rhetorical choice.
- **EQ4.** The shift in Q4's source-answer at v11 (from the LORD's own direct first-person acts, vv4-9, to the people's own reflexive self-directed acts, "appoint for themselves") — worth tracking whether Hosea's restoration oracles elsewhere in the book continue to give the restored people their own agency, or whether this is a one-off structural note.
